item: Gates G24 (deployment and release qualification) and G25 (status and evidence consistency) for kudurru v0.2.0, PR #54 at HEAD 33ee04bc
summary: G24 and G25 are both still open in the tracker (dev-docs/milestones/v0.2/completion-plan.md:223-224; closure rules in gaps.md:113-114), and almost all of what remains is evidence recording and documentation, not product code. Version sync is done: VERSION is 0.2.0, both charts are 0.2.0 (deploy/helm/kudurru/Chart.yaml:5-6, deploy/helm/kudurru-crds/Chart.yaml:5-6), Compose/kustomize images are 0.2.0, and `make version-check` printed PASS when I ran it at 33ee04bc. All 10 hosted PR workflows are green on the current head 33ee04bc (ci 42736964083, compose 42736963783, kind 42736964167, edge 42736964064, security 42736963918, docs 42736963880, license-server 42736964088, dev-image 42736963883, website, ad-dns; only the owner-excluded Cloudflare "Workers Builds: kudurru-docs" fails), but the tracker records none of this: its newest hosted entry is the failed CI 42568583609 on ffd18d41 and it still says final-source hosted checks remain (completion-plan.md:1763-1779). The tracker has no recorded result at all for compose-e2e, kind-e2e, helm-check, edge-check, release-manifests, goreleaser or version-check (zero grep hits in completion-plan.md, gaps.md and followup-audit.md); `make size` is recorded only for 19d6c729 (completion-plan.md:235-236), while the hosted build job on 33ee04bc measured 81,146,016 bytes with the placeholder dashboard. CHANGELOG.md has a `## [0.2.0] - unreleased` section (line 133), but the D355-D366 entries sit in a separate `## [Unreleased]` section above it (lines 7-131), the 0.2.0 section has two `### Fixed` blocks (135, 466), many stale "remains pending" clauses, a stray paragraph (510-513), no upgrade notes or known limitations, and no entries for a long list of landed features. The PR #54 body contradicts itself and the code in at least five places (for example it says Kubernetes RFC 2136 "needs an owner decision" although D366 shipped in 33ee04bc). Operator docs exist for most new flows (docs/deploy/sqlite-join.md, tsig-keys.md, compose-ha.md, runbooks.md, integrations.md) but are not linked from docs/deploy/README.md, lack first-primary activation and promotion steps, lack an RFC 2136 operator page, and several pages still state v0.1-era limits. The uncommitted dashboard/dist/index.html is a locally built dashboard index (output of `make dashboard-build`); it must never be committed and should be restored to the placeholder with `git checkout -- dashboard/dist/index.html`. This sandbox has no Docker daemon (`docker info` fails), no kind, goreleaser, kustomize or golangci-lint on PATH, so Compose/kind/edge/image checks can only be qualified through hosted runs.

remaining.title: Live-internet recursion check and IANA trust-anchor comparison
remaining.detail: release-checklist.md:252-259 (D170): `KUDURRU_LIVE_DNS=1 go test -run TestLiveInternet ./internal/recursor` (gate at internal/recursor/resolver_test.go:630-631) and a comparison of the built-in anchors (internal/recursor/roots.go:47-51, key tags 20326 and 38696; internal/dnssec/options.go:46) with IANA root-anchors.xml. The tracker explicitly says this acceptance is not inferred (gaps.md:3431-3432). It needs outbound UDP and TCP port 53 and HTTPS to data.iana.org, nothing owner-specific; try it here first and fall back to any network that allows port 53 egress. The on-node `dig +dnssec` half (254-257) needs a running node with a recursive group and can use the same environment. It is a GA gate per release-checklist.md:178-179, so if it cannot run before merge it is recorded as a known gap, not as passed.
remaining.acceptance: release-checklist.md:252-259. Proof: unskipped TestLiveInternet pass output; the two DS digests match the current IANA file; result recorded with date, since anchors are time-sensitive.

remaining.title: Restore the built dashboard index to the committed placeholder
remaining.detail: `git diff dashboard/dist/index.html` replaces the placeholder (marker `<!-- kudurru:placeholder -->`, dashboard/embed.go:45) with a Vite-built index that references ./assets/index-CI8jxBgG.js and about 20 other hashed files. Those files exist locally (121 files in dashboard/dist/assets) but are gitignored (.gitignore:13-14). It is the output of `make dashboard-build`. d47c9fc0 committed it by mistake together with TEMPDIAG diagnostics and c50adc9f reverted both 13 minutes later. Committing it would break CI: TestIndexAssetsPresent fails when index.html references files that are not embedded (dashboard/embed_test.go:45-60), and the checklist says not to commit it (release-checklist.md:103). It should be reverted, not committed: `git checkout -- dashboard/dist/index.html` (release-checklist.md:150-152). The tracker calls it a 'protected pre-existing' modification (completion-plan.md:1490, 1761) and the PR body mentions it (line 34), so restoring it is a one-line ledger note plus removing that sentence from the PR body. It is harmless while unstaged (all drift checks are path-scoped: Makefile:179,185; ci.yml:449), but any `git add -A` or `git commit -a` would re-create the d47c9fc0 mistake, and non-snapshot goreleaser refuses a dirty tree (.goreleaser.yaml:15-17). It is regenerated by `make dashboard-build` whenever a real-bundle test is wanted. Run `make clean` as well if a placeholder-only build is needed, since leftover assets are still embedded (dashboard/embed.go:29-30, `all:dist`).
remaining.acceptance: release-checklist.md:103 and 150-152. Proof: `git status --short` prints nothing; `git show HEAD:dashboard/dist/index.html | grep -c kudurru:placeholder` is 1.

recommendation:
Treat G24/G25 as one final pass that runs after the other items stop changing code, and do it in two commits plus one PR-body edit. The order matters because a commit cannot contain its own hosted results.

Runbook:
1. Preconditions. `git status --short` shows only ` M dashboard/dist/index.html`. Stage explicit paths only; never `git add -A` or `git commit -a` (that is how d47c9fc0 happened). Commits need `Signed-off-by` (CONTRIBUTING.md:25) and American English (CLAUDE.md).
2. Optional small code commit first: wire hack/test_sync_version.py into ci.yml (G24-SYNCTEST) and, if chosen, the label-triggered release dry-run workflow (G24-SNAPSHOT option B). Push. This is the code head C.
3. Local checks at C that need no Docker (save output under .context/release-checks-<date>/): `make version-check` (expect PASS); `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s hack -p test_sync_version.py`; `hack/release-tag.sh rc` (expect tag=v0.2.0-rc.1); `make check-generated` (no diff; docs-gen took 41 s in gaps.md:6833); `make deploy-tools && make release-manifests RELEASE_ARTIFACT_VERSION=0.2.0-rc.1` then inspect bin/release image tags; `make dashboard-build && go test -count=1 ./dashboard/... && make size` (record bytes against the 100,000,000 budget); `go run github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/v2@v2.18.3 build --snapshot --single-target --clean` and `./dist/kudurru_linux_amd64_v1/kudurru version`; then `git checkout -- dashboard/dist/index.html && rm -rf dist` and confirm `git status --short` is empty (G24-TREE; the built index is reproducible, so restoring it loses nothing).
4. Try `KUDURRU_LIVE_DNS=1 go test -run TestLiveInternet ./internal/recursor` and compare the two root DS records with IANA; if port 53 egress is blocked, record it as an open GA gate.
5. Wait for the 10 hosted workflows on C (about 47 minutes; go test 1/2 is the long pole at 45 minutes). Save `gh run list --commit <C> --json databaseId,workflowName,conclusion,headSha` to .context/hosted-<C>-<date>/runs.json. Rerun and record any transient download failure.
6. One docs commit: ledgers with the commit map and C's results (G25-LEDGER), package acceptance table (G25-PACKAGES), CHANGELOG (G25-CHANGELOG), README and progress text (G25-ROADMAP), operator docs (G25-OPDOCS), followups (G25-FOLLOWUPS). Before committing: `make docs-gen` (no diff), `make docs-site`, `make docs-check-links`, `python3 hack/guide-lint.py`, `make version-check`.
7. Push the docs commit. It re-runs the full suite because the change filter diffs the whole PR. When green, put the final head's run IDs in the PR description with `gh pr edit 54 --body-file` (G25-PRBODY); this creates no commit, so nothing re-runs.
8. Do not tag, push release-candidate or release, publish, or date the changelog.

Design choices I would make without asking the owner, recorded as D367 onward: keep `## [0.2.0] - unreleased` and fold `[Unreleased]` into it (follows release-checklist.md:116-120 and the sync script's own heading logic); classify the owner-hardware checklist items as open GA gates using the checklist's own rule (178-179) and the D353/D358 precedent of recording deferrals as 'unqualified, not passed'; close the full goreleaser snapshot with a label-triggered workflow, following the benchmarks.yml precedent of a `pull_request: types: [labeled]` trigger so it can run before the workflow reaches the default branch (.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml:10-13); and restore the dashboard index rather than keep carrying a 'protected' dirty file. The D366 pattern (record the decision in one commit, 19bfecc4, then implement, 33ee04bc) is the model for any of these that change behavior. D138/D75 govern the size record and D154 the volume check on the snapshot images.

designOptions.name: A. Partial local dry run, full snapshot at candidate time
designOptions.description: Run `goreleaser check` (already hosted), the single-target snapshot build and `make release-manifests` locally without Docker; record the full `goreleaser release --snapshot` as not run and leave it to the first release candidate publish.
designOptions.pros: No new code; matches the M5 historical record that the checklist accepts for an rc (release-checklist.md:157-158); pipeline files barely changed on this branch.
designOptions.cons: G24 asks for artifact validation; archives, deb/rpm/apk, SBOMs and ko images stay unvalidated until something is published, which is exactly when a failure is most expensive.

designOptions.name: B. Label-triggered release dry-run workflow (recommended)
designOptions.description: Add .github/workflows/release-dry-run.yml with `workflow_dispatch` and `pull_request: types: [labeled]` (label `release-dry-run`), running goreleaser v2.18.3 `release --snapshot --clean --skip=publish,sign` with Bun and syft v1.54.1, `kudurru version` in both ko images, hack/volume-check.sh on them, and uploading the artifact listing. No registry login, read-only token.
designOptions.pros: Real artifact validation on a Docker runner before merge; repeatable for every later release; follows the benchmarks.yml labeled-trigger precedent; publishes nothing.
designOptions.cons: One more workflow to maintain and pin (TestWorkflowActionsPinned applies); adds a code commit and one more full hosted cycle to the final pass; signing is still not exercised (needs the release-branch OIDC identity).

designOptions.name: C. Manual run on a Docker-capable machine
designOptions.description: Someone with Docker, goreleaser and syft runs the snapshot by hand at the frozen head and pastes the result into the ledger, as in the v0.1 fix round (release-checklist.md:159-168).
designOptions.cons: Not possible in this sandbox (no Docker daemon); depends on another machine and is not reproducible by reviewers.

risks: A commit cannot record its own hosted results: the ledger can only cite the last code head, and the final head's run IDs must live in the PR description. If any code lands after the ledger commit, the recorded qualification is stale again.

The three ledgers mirror each other and every parallel item appends to all of them plus CHANGELOG.md and the decision log; the G25 restructuring will conflict with any item still in flight. D-number collisions are likely (next free D367).

G25 cannot claim feature completion while any of the 11 packages is unaccepted. Greps for this map found no code for dnstap, OTel tracing, ClickHouse/Loki sinks, the `external` zone type, a dashboard join wizard or Integrations page, or a Corefile importer; README.md:107 currently promises 'dnstap and tracing' for v0.2.0. These were surface greps, not a full audit of those packages.

The managed-anchor hosted failure was fixed by reordering the test (a7e70b22). Its commit message describes real behavior: a startup DNSZone status write after first readiness makes the zone briefly unavailable and drops in-flight answers from the retired publication, by design under D313/D332. If that is recorded only as a fixture fix, a user-visible startup window goes undocumented; it belongs in the ledger and probably in Known limitations.

No Docker in this sandbox: Compose, kind, edge, image scans and the full goreleaser snapshot depend entirely on hosted runs. Hosted tool downloads have returned 504 before (completion-plan.md:1697-1702, 1763-1765), so reruns may be needed and must be recorded, not treated as passes.
go test shard 1/2 takes 45 minutes against 12 for shard 2/2; each final-pass iteration costs about 47 minutes of wall time, and the shard weights in hack/go-test-shard.sh are from October.

The dirty dashboard/dist/index.html can be committed by accident with a broad `git add`; that fails TestIndexAssetsPresent in CI. While it is present, local `make build` and `make size` embed the real bundle, so local size numbers differ from the hosted placeholder figure (81,146,016 bytes on 33ee04bc).

Binary size grew from 57,991,328 bytes at v0.1 (Makefile:56-58) to about 81 MB. It is inside the 100,000,000 budget, but D138 expects growth to be explained; the real-bundle size at the head is unrecorded.

`make version-check` also verifies image references inside README, docs/deploy, docs/guide and docs-site/content/start (hack/sync-version.py:104-108); new or edited doc pages with image tags must use 0.2.0 or the helm job fails. Prose that says 'v0.1.0' is not touched by the sync and needs manual editing.

docs.kudurru.io deploys from the `release` branch through Cloudflare Workers Builds, whose check currently fails and is excluded by the owner. The hosted `docs` workflow (including `wrangler deploy --dry-run`) is green, but if the Cloudflare failure is a real build problem, corrected operator docs will not publish at promotion.

Pages scoped to 'v0.1.0' (docs/guide/README.md:34, docs-site/content/_index.md:19, migrate pages) describe the published release; changing the framing before GA would misdescribe what users can install, while leaving feature facts stale misdescribes the branch. The split between 'fix facts now' and 'flip framing at GA' needs to be applied consistently.
followups.md rows may only be retargeted by the owner (followups.md:13-15); closing rows whose package is not accepted would overstate completion.
